title: Unity worth it?
author: Saytron3030
selftext:
Has anyone developed with Claude and Unity that can speak to the experience?

I made https://mekkor.io with Phaser JS because it just works on any browser. If I am making a simple game without 3D models or anything is worth using Unity at all?

In the past I hated Unity because of how much I had to open the Unity App and click around. Is the MCP basically handling all of that? Is it essentially writing just C# code?

Curious people's thoughts

comments.author: wewerecreaturres
comments.body: i just use direct cli tools instead of the mcp, but yeah i dont have to open unity at all for claude to make edits to things, but like...if you dont even want to go as far as to open unity to click a couple of things, maybe you shouldnt be making games.

replies.author: Vivid-Snow-2089
replies.body: why? opening unity and navigating its UI has nothing to do with user ideation and wanting a game of something

replies.author: Saytron3030
replies.body: Why even use Unity though opposed to just going straight to C# code or something, what does it offer that can't be built natively

replies.author: wewerecreaturres
replies.body: You gonna build your own engine?

replies.author: Saytron3030
replies.body: If there are no physics involved why not?

replies.author: wewerecreaturres
replies.body: So then you have the answer to your question already. Why ask?

replies.author: Other-Environment986
replies.body: At that point its about the engine. Sure you can ask claude to build a custom engine for your game. But you will be wasting tokens & time on something that could be done in godot, unreal & unity in way less time.

comments.body: I’m curious too. What is the advantage of using unity?

replies.author: Other-Environment986
replies.body: Essentially the tooling that comes with it. Your ai will have access to the full arsenal that comes with unity. Same with godot & unreal. Either way I recommend learning atleast some of the engine you will be working in regardless of how much ai you plan to use.

comments.author: erratic_ostrich
comments.body:
>Has anyone developed with Claude and Unity that can speak to the experience?

I did, it's pretty fucking awesome.

>If I am making a simple game without 3D models or anything is worth using Unity at all?

If it's really that simple, then probably not. The advantage of unity is all the built-in functionalities plus third party assets, all of it fine tuned over years of real usage. Most JS frameworks like phaser need to write most of that from scratch. But if Phaser has been working fine for you so far then maybe that's all you need.

>In the past I hated Unity because of how much I had to open the Unity App and click around. Is the MCP basically handling all of that? Is it essentially writing just C# code?

MCP can handle pretty much everything, not just code. But you would still need to open the editor sometimes and also a basic understanding of how unity works.

  
In short, AI reduced unity's learning curve by 99%, if you are not willing to do the other 1% and just want to do simple games then a simple JS framework is good enough.

replies.author: Saytron3030
replies.body: Thank you I think this is what I needed. I was thinking even C++

replies.author: iolmao
replies.body: What's the token consumption of MCP for unity?

comments.author: wirthmore
comments.body:
Unity is free for indie developers, supports a lot of already solved issues, and is a swiss-army-knife. 

The Unity MCP is capable of a lot, yes you can just write a lot of scripts, although I live in the Unity Editor and hand tweak everything at all times anyway, so I'm a bad judge of whether you could forego ever opening Unity. It's much faster to tweak URP settings than telling Claude to do it, for example. (Note the "telling Claude" is slow, not Claude doing it)
